crime: Each morning in the lounge, one girl braided everyone's hair and tucked in a flower she picked in the field. At home she had done her five little sisters' hair before school. Each morning she asked {WITCH_NAME} too and was snapped at.
When it rained, {WITCH_NAME} walked to the flower field alone under a roof of hardened air. Rain sheeted off its invisible edges; no one followed.

One rainy morning, as the doors unlocked, the girl ducked under that roof and walked out with her. There she braided {WITCH_NAME}'s hair, tying it off with her ribbon and a flower. "Just once. No one can see us out here."

{WITCH_NAME}'s mother had braided her hair once, on her last night home, tying it with her own ribbon. By morning she was gone, the ribbon still in her daughter's hair. Anyone who turned gentle all at once was already leaving.

{WITCH_NAME} pulled the ribbon from her braid, looped it around the girl's throat and held on until the girl lay still, face down on the soaked ground. She walked back under a new roof and left the first standing over the body, rain still sheeting off it onto the flowers.
She came to breakfast in the dining hall before the rain stopped, dry as always, and sat with the girls until the body was found.

The rain stopped, the girl never came to braid, and the prisoners found her face down among the flowers, strangled with her own ribbon, back dry, front soaked. They assumed she had gone out after the rain, when {WITCH_NAME} was already at breakfast.

Picking flowers for her there, a prisoner found four straight furrows beaten into the mud around the spot, like drip lines under a roof that wasn't there. At trial they saw it: a roof had shed the rain around her as it fell. She had died in the rain, under a roof {WITCH_NAME} left behind.
fields.epitaph: It was never goodbye. She would have braided it again tomorrow.
fields.epithet: Hair No Gentle Hand May Braid
execution: From the top of the trial court, the execution stand lowers a giant braid of hair. Its tip is plaited around her ankles and tied off with a ribbon, and she hangs from it head down.
The braid plaits itself tighter, twist by twist, winding her up to the top of the court.
Then it comes undone, strand by strand, from the top down. The last strands loosen around her ankles and let her go. She drops headfirst onto the stone floor.
The ribbon drifts down onto her still body. Above her, only the loose hair sways.

magic.name: Walls of Thin Air
magic.text: She hardens the air around her into invisible walls no one and nothing can push through.
